gaps.what: The regenerated RI-CMB07 exemplar is a 120-second, 7200-frame fight in which the player is never hit. Measured from the shipped statistics file and independently recomputed from the JSONL: swings taken 0 (band 0.05-0.35), damage taken / max HP 0 (band 0.4-1.6), player hp at fight end 620/620, frames at exactly 0 stamina 0 (band 20-600), mean stamina 0.8303 (band 0.55-0.80), 45.87% of frames above 90% stamina (band 0.12-0.45), whiff rate 0.72 (band 0.03-0.25), swings negated by i-frames 0.115 (band 0.4-0.8), longest committed run 155 f (band 180-520), punish-window usage rate null. Eleven of twenty-four banded rows are out of band against RI-CMB07 M2's floor of at most four, over one fight against a floor of five. Of the enemy's 26 swings, 11.5% were dodged and 7.7% blocked; the other 81% simply missed.
gaps.why_it_matters: The exemplar is the artifact RI-CMB03 M7, RI-CMB05 §B, RI-CMB09 §3 and RI-AI03 all diff against, so a fight with no danger in it makes every one of those checks pass for the wrong reason and hides the real defects underneath - the guard-break window that regenerates stamina and the hitstun lengths that are six frames long, neither of which the exemplar could ever have exposed because the player is never guard-broken and never staggered in it.

remedy.action: Rewrite the exemplar bot in tools/harness/cmb-exemplar.mjs so it fights inside the enemy's reach band instead of drifting out of it: hold 1.2-2.2 m from the target during ATK_WINDUP rather than retreating, commit to a punish inside every declared recovery window, and take the trade when stamina is short instead of walking away. Add an explicit assertion pass that refuses to write the exemplar unless it clears RI-CMB07 M2, and generate five seeded fights and take the row-wise median as the item requires.
remedy.acceptance: Over the row-wise median of five seeded fights: at least 20 of the 24 banded rows inside band, with rows 13 (swings taken) in 0.05-0.35, 14 (damage taken / max HP) in 0.4-1.6, 16 (frames at exactly 0 stamina) in 20-600, 17 in 0.03-0.20, 18 in 0.12-0.45, 19 in 0.55-0.80 and 25 in 180-520 all inside band individually, row 27 (punish-window usage rate) a number in 0.50-0.95 rather than null, and at least one GUARD_BREAK and one stagger present in the trace so RI-CMB03 M5 and RI-CMB05 M3 have something to measure.

gaps.what: The entire Writ House creation sequence renders nothing. Driving all 19 census nodes through window.__HARNESS and screenshotting after each at 1920x1080 produces 20 byte-identical PNGs (sha256 7277a273453ac8631c318f3d9120d7b12b7f562b187adabf59fe3ca7b5daaeb5) showing a body standing in an empty green field: no barge hold, no Writ House interior, no Jeeh-Ei, no Warden-Scribe Tuleeh-Ma, no question, no answer options, and document.body.innerText empty at every node. listEntities() returns 0 entities before and after creation. The scene exists only as a JSON state machine whose getCensusState() self-reports full_screen:false, world_visible:true and full_screen_panels:0 — three fields with no rendered counterpart. RI-CHR01's first bar is 'creation is a scene, not a screen'; what shipped is neither, and RI-JRN01's whole Diegesis block (35 of its 100 points) has nothing to measure.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player starting this game is never asked anything by anybody: the best-written material in the piece — a bored official who guesses your race wrong and tells you the sex box changes nothing because he has watched for eleven years — is delivered to no one, so character creation cannot be experienced at all.

remedy.action: Render the census scene over the live 3D view. (1) In game/data/states/writ-house.json, place the two NPC entities the scene already names — jeeh-ei in the barge hold and warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma behind the desk — as real entities with positions and the npcs/writ-house.json records attached, so listEntities() returns >= 2 throughout creation and the speaker named by getCensusState().speaker has a body in the frame. (2) Add a dialogue surface to game/src/render that draws getCensusState()'s `line`, `input.kind` and `input.options` as a bottom-anchored panel occupying <= 55% of frame area with the world rendering behind it, and drives censusAnswer() from real input (press/release on the closed action set, so keyboard, gamepad and touch all work). (3) Move the camera to the interior named in getCensusState().interior for the duration of the scene. (4) Render readWrit() as an openable inventory object rather than a string returned by an API.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run tools/harness/critic-w1-07a.mjs. RI-JRN01 M5/M6 then become measurable and the item can leave 0.

gaps.what: The effect catalogue is a complete, correctly priced, deterministic parameter space with one behaviour behind it. Measured across all 71 shipped spells: 5 of 55 effects produce the mechanical consequence their own record describes (fire, frost, shock and poison damage, and damage_health); 1 is partial (levitate meters altitude and charges 1.5 Focus/m but never moves pos[1]); 16 resolve only as HP damage equal to their own magnitude — demoralise deals 111 hp and the enemy stays AGGRO, calm_beast deals 31 hp and the beast stays in COMBAT, open_lock deals 31 hp to a creature, charm 184, corrode 310, lock_lock 184, silence 31, paralyse 12 with no buildup field on the enemy record at all; and 33 are a row in effects_active that no other system in the build reads — shield and resist_element each mitigate 0 of a scripted 100-damage hit, the_greater_mending heals 0 with the player at 420 of 620, feather leaves equip_load_pct at 24 and roll_class at LIGHT, fortify_skill satisfies no gate, bind_lesser summons nothing (entity count 0 to 0), wall creates no collider, leap adds 0 m of altitude, recall completes its 210-frame ritual and leaves the player at exactly the coordinates it started from, hist_sight completes and writes 0 journal entries, and all five Veiling effects leave getStealthState() byte-identical to baseline against the stealth system shipping in the same build.
gaps.why_it_matters: S19 says spell effects are tools and quests must be solvable with them, so a player who buys the Open spell to get past the warded door in The Warded Ledger will instead do thirty-one points of damage to the door's guard, and the >=45% non-combat resolution bar that magic is supposed to supply a fifth of is satisfied only in JSON.

remedy.action: Replace the single generic applicator with a per-effect handler registry. Concretely: (1) In game/src/sim/combat-bridge.js, the spell-contact callback currently accumulates `dmg += outputOf(effect, magnitude)` for every effect whose utility_class is null OR whose geometry is not 'none' — restrict that accumulation to the five damage effects (fire_damage, frost_damage, shock_damage, poison_damage, damage_health) plus the status buildup each declares, so a non-damage effect can never deal HP damage. (2) Add game/src/sim/magic/apply.js: a table keyed by effect id, one handler per effect, called from MagicSystem.applyEffects(), each handler writing into the system RI-MAG06 §B names for that effect. (3) Wire the eight consumers that already exist in this build before touching anything that does not: CombatBody.equipLoadPct/tier for feather and burden (RI-CMB01's 30.00/70.00 cliff must stay exactly where it is); CombatBody.hp for restore_health, drain_health and absorb_health, and hpMax for drain; a mitigation multiplier ahead of the damage write for shield, resist_element and sap_ward; sim.stealth.d.detection's V terms and sound radius for chameleon (clamped 80), invisibility (breaking on attack, cast, interact, container and COMBAT), muffle, night_eye and false_face; the S11 buildup meter for paralyse, so it crosses a threshold instead of arriving in one frame; enemy alert_state and the leash for calm_beast, demoralise and frenzy, ending COMBAT with zero death events; CombatBody.pos for mark/recall/intervention, so a completed ritual actually moves the player; and a real locomotion mode for levitate that writes pos[1], caps horizontal speed at 1.4 m/s and drops light, heavy, block, roll and parry. (4) Every effect whose consuming system genuinely does not exist yet (water bands, the lock register, item condition, the quest knowledge store) gets an explicit UNMEASURABLE row in the census naming the piece that owns it, capped at five per RI-MAG06 M6.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run RI-MAG06's census (reference implementation at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-14/consolidate.mjs). EFFECT-FUNCTION >= 50/55; HP_DAMAGE_ONLY == 0 (hard fail above 3); UNREAD_TIMER <= 2; UNMEASURABLE <= 5, each naming its owning piece. Plus these five named single-trace assertions, each of which fails today: still_the_beast on an aggroed beast_slitherfang ends COMBAT with alert_state != AGGRO and zero death events; feather moves roll_class across RI-CMB01's 30.00% cliff with the discontinuity still at exactly 30.00; thick_skin reduces a scripted 100-damage hit by the declared fraction; the_deep_chameleon changes getStealthState().V; recall moves getPlayerStats().pos to the mark.

gaps.what: The seeded PRNG is reseeded correctly and never drawn from. rng.draws is 0 on every one of 3600 frames in every scenario, state and seed measured. Seeds 1337 and 4242 over a 3600-frame duel differ in exactly one field — .rng.seed, the echo of the input — and in zero simulation fields (r4-seed-sensitivity.txt: 'frames differing in ANY field other than .rng.seed: 0'). RI-MTH02 R4's 5%-of-frames clause is therefore satisfied at 100% by that echo alone, so the rung, tools/harness/determinism.mjs, and any future critic reading either will report seed sensitivity on a build that has none. The build's own ladder prints 'PASS R4 — seed-sensitive ... frames_differing_pct: 100'.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every downstream claim of seeded variety — RI-AI01 M4's inter-COMMIT coefficient of variation, rumours that differ per town, seeded loot placement — is unfalsifiable until the seed reaches something, and the corpus's own detector for that condition currently returns PASS.

remedy.action: (1) Route at least one simulation quantity through rng.next() inside the fixed step and emit the draw count truthfully — the enemy idle-loop phase offset chosen at spawn is sufficient, cheap, and is exactly the field AM-W1-00-01 wants excluded from R5, so seeding it converts that argument into a measurement. (2) Change tools/harness/determinism.mjs's R4 computation to drop the rng.seed field before counting differing frames, and to fail the rung with reason 'prng_never_drawn' when max(rng.draws) == 0 in either run. (3) Adopt orchestration/amendments/AM-W1-00-C1-mth02-r4-discriminator.md, which states the sharpened rung and moves no threshold.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run node tools/harness/trace.mjs --scenario cmb-duel-infantry at seeds 1337 and 4242 and diff field-by-field: max(rng.draws) > 0 in both runs, and >= 5% of frames differ in at least one field OTHER than .rng.seed. The second number is currently 0.0% (0 of 3600 frames) and is recorded in r4-seed-sensitivity.txt.

gaps.what: The save does not carry enemies[].prev_state. RI-JRN05 M5 run as written — identical 120-frame pre-roll on both sides, identical 600-frame script, seed 4711, control vs loaded — gives control body_sha256 5d0830f9b9e3ea71… and loaded d52edb76370c7c08…, differing on 219 of 600 frames in exactly that field: control "IDLE", loaded null, from frame 0 onward. The serialised entity record carries state, anim_frame, anim_phase0 and state_entered_ago_frames and stops there. world.entities is a durable path in game/data/save-manifest.json and prev_state is on no volatile list, so manifest rule V1 makes it a defect by the manifest's own terms. The same probe against round-1 commit 8714e38 reproduces it exactly, so it is pre-existing and was missed by both the build and the previous verdict, which recorded M5 as passing.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player who reloads gets an enemy whose state history has been erased, so the first transition after a reload is taken from a different predecessor than the one the unsaved game would have used — RI-JRN05's own "how we lose" #5: nothing a player does catches it until a boss behaves differently after a reload.

remedy.action: Serialise prev_state in the entity record next to state and state_entered_ago_frames and restore it in the load path; add prev_state to the World group field list in game/data/save-manifest.json so RI-JRN05 M4's two-directional set-difference covers it; and extend the R9 rung and RI-JRN05 M5 to compare the full field set of the control and loaded traces rather than only body_sha256 of a window, printing the differing field names — round 1's M5 run passed precisely because it did not.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run RI-JRN05 M5 (or corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-00-r2/p10-m5.mjs) at seed 4711 and at one other seed: the control and loaded traces must have identical body_sha256 after re-basing the absolute frame indices, and the field-level diff must be EMPTY. Today it is {"enemies[].prev_state": 219} of 600 frames.

gaps.what: The 87 authored movesets are unreachable from the running game. setLoadout() rejects all 87 roster ids with 'no moveset <id>. Known: axe, dagger, greatsword, halberd, spear, straight-sword, ultra-greatsword', and eight of the fifteen classes (CSW TSW FST MCE WHP CGS GHM BOW) have no live representation at all. What a player can press is game/data/combat/spine/*.json, which declares three slots — light, heavy, two_handed{light,heavy} — so every weapon in the game plays exactly four distinct animation ids. Measured consequences: CFS_live = 0.0000 with 20 of 20 (weapon x contextual state) combinations playing the standing r1.1 clip byte-identically; distinct_anim = 4 against RI-WPN01 M3's floor of 18; RI-WPN01 M6 declared-vs-observed agreement 0.5357 with the clip id — the field RI-WPN01 §B calls 'the load-bearing field of the whole weapons area' — matching on 0 of 14 rows.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every weapon in the game is the same weapon: four attacks, and rolling, backstepping, sprinting, jumping and guard-countering all play the standing light attack, which is exactly the failure the user named when they asked for this piece.

remedy.action: Make MovesetLibrary the runtime's move source instead of a harness-only reader. (1) In game/src/combat/system.js createPlayer(), build the move table from game/data/combat/movesets/*.json via MovesetLibrary rather than from game/data/combat/spine/*.json, so setLoadout({weapon:'ssw_garrison_sword'}) resolves. (2) In game/src/combat/player.js, dispatch the attack buttons through MovesetLibrary.resolveSlot(weaponId, button, ctx) with ctx carrying state, state_frame, roll_tier, stance, offhand and descending/fall_height, and delete the code path that falls through to the standing light attack when no window matches — a missed window must produce nothing, per RI-WPN04 §B rule 2. (3) Add player.anim_slot, player.hitstop_f and player.weapon_tip to the frame record and a block_success event to the trace vocabulary. (4) Restore the R2 active/recovery split of the seven spine classes to game/data/combat/frames.json, which RI-WPN02 §B's authority note makes binding. (5) Repair the 82 weapons whose chains_to points at a slot they do not declare (50x 2h.r2 -> 2h.r2.follow, 32x r2 -> r2.follow, 4x r1.3 -> r1.4).
targets: game/data/states/ (add wpn-dummy-arena, wpn-material-range, wpn-loadout-o1_sword_shield, wpn-loadout-o2_dual, wpn-loadout-o3_twohand)

gaps.what: The trunk road network is routed along the floors of water bodies. Sampling getWaterAt() at every point of all ten built legs at tide LOW: 1,364 m of road (5.4%) is above knee depth and 574 m (2.3%) is above chest depth, concentrated on the Stormhold-Helstrom leg, which carries 538 m over-knee and 502 m over-chest and reaches a maximum depth of 65.64 m at (2182.52, 2214.63) - ground at 69.66 m under a water surface at 135.30 m. That leg is the first of THE CROSSING, so 502 m of the canonical 6,788 m walk - 7.4%, about 4.2 minutes of the hour - is walked along a lake bed. The player traverses it at 2.0000 m/s in state WALK at full HP and full stamina, with no swim, no wade band, no breath clock and no drowning; a screenshot from that point is a uniformly black-green frame of water volume. Nothing in the instrument suite asks the question: scale-audit.mjs has a TIDEWAY-INVERSION check that measures water depth on exactly one of the ten legs and none on the other nine.
gaps.why_it_matters: The 56.574-minute crossing that every density figure in the corpus is denominated in is measured along a route that stops being walkable the moment RI-WLD10's depth bands land - 502 m at the declared swim speed of 1.1 m/s is 7.6 minutes underwater against a 40-60 second breath clock - so the traversal minute is resting on water having no effect, and a player walking the main road today sees a black screen for four minutes.

remedy.action: Add water depth to the trunk-routing cost in tools/world/build-roads.mjs: make any cell whose water depth exceeds 0.60 m (band W2) impassable to A*, except on the leg RI-WLD01 §4 declares 'tideway', and re-run the build chain build-terrain -> build-water-hazards -> build-roads. Where a leg genuinely must cross a channel, emit a bridge or causeway deck into game/data/world/roads.json as a raised polyline carrying its own surface height, so the road is over the water rather than under it. Then add the check that does not exist to tools/world/scale-audit.mjs as M2-ROAD-ABOVE-WATER, covering all ten legs at all four tide phases rather than one leg at one phase.

Then add the check that does not exist to tools/world/scale-audit.mjs as M2-ROAD-ABOVE-WATER, covering all ten legs at all four tide phases rather than one leg at one phase.
gaps.remedy_acceptance: tools/world/scale-audit.mjs reports 0 m of trunk road above band W2 on every leg except lilmoth-archon, at all four tide phases (RISING, HIGH, FALLING, LOW); lilmoth-archon keeps its declared inversion at <=0.85 m deep at LOW and >=1.40 m at HIGH; and tools/world/crossing.mjs re-measures the crossing on the re-routed network inside 52-65 min and 6,300-7,600 m with mean ground speed still 2.00 +/-0.05 m/s.
